Cryptococcal meningitis: an antifungal induction network that does not connect, and a separate trial of when to start antiretroviral therapy

Among randomised trials in HIV-associated cryptococcal meningitis, what does each antifungal induction trial report for ten-week mortality, can those trials be joined into a network, and what does the separate trial of antiretroviral timing report?

risk ratio computed here from the two counts on this row, with a normal-approximation interval on the log scale. Death is the outcome, so a ratio below one means fewer deaths on the first-named treatment.		Primary paper (abstract only; full text behind a paywall):
Mortality in the oral-regimen, 1-week amphotericin B, and 2-week amphotericin B groups was 18.2% (41 of 225), 21.9% (49 of 224), and 21.4% (49 of 229), respectively, at 2 weeks and was 35.1% (79 of 225), 36.2% (81 of 224), and 39.7% (91 of 229), respectively, at 10 weeks.

This contrast comes from a trial that randomised three strategies at once, so it shares whole arms with the trial's other contrasts, and sharing an arm means sharing those participants and their deaths. It shares the two-week strategy with the contrast of the one-week strategy against the two-week strategy. It shares the oral strategy with the contrast of the oral strategy against the one-week strategy. Each contrast is valid alone. Entering any of them alongside another as though it were a separate study would count the shared participants twice, which is why nothing here is added. Note this is not only a shared-REFERENCE-arm problem: one of these three contrasts never touches the trial's reference arm at all and still shares participants with both others.

The methods rule governing this decision

Decision: No network estimate and no indirect comparison is computed for antifungal induction.

Cochrane Handbook sections: 11.2.1, 11.2.2, 11.3.2.3, 11.4.4.1

Section 11.2.1 describes an indirect comparison as one made through a common comparator. These trials share no node, so that construction has no input. Whether a shared node could be forced into being by treating the one-week strategy as though it were the flucytosine-partnered regimen is a question about node grouping, and section 11.3.2.3 is what governs it: node definitions need careful consideration and should maximise similarity within a node. Half of that strategy received a different partner drug, and within that very node the trial demonstrated a difference: flucytosine better than fluconazole on ten-week mortality, with an interval excluding no effect. An earlier version called that the difference the trial found to matter most, which ranks it against strategy comparisons the trial reported as non-inferiority conclusions on a different window; the source states no such ranking and a reviewer was right to strike it. A demonstrated difference inside the node is enough on its own, so the two are not one node. An earlier version of this block argued that point from transitivity alone and a reviewer was right that transitivity does not settle what a node is. Once the nodes are fixed, section 11.2.2 refuses the forced merge for its own reason: it requires the sets of trials to be similar in all important factors other than the comparison being made, and half of that node received a different partner drug, which is the one difference the trial demonstrated inside that node, on its own ten-week mortality comparison. No claim is made that it mattered more than anything else the trial tested; that would rank a superiority finding against non-inferiority conclusions on another window, which the source does not do. On loops, an earlier version of this object said the graph closed none. It does close one, and a reviewer was right to say so: the multi-arm trial supplies all three pairwise lines among its own strategies, which is the triangle section 11.1.1 describes a three-arm study as drawing. That loop still buys NO incoherence check, and the reason is not its absence but its provenance. Section 11.4.4.1 defines incoherence as the difference between the direct and the indirect estimate of the same comparison; here the indirect path runs through the third node of the same randomised population, so it is not independent evidence about the direct edge -- it is the same participants, arriving a different way. Comparing them would measure arithmetic, not disagreement between sources.

The methods rule governing this decision

Decision: No network estimate and no indirect comparison is computed for antifungal induction.

Cochrane Handbook sections: 11.2.1, 11.2.2, 11.3.2.3, 11.4.4.1

Section 11.2.1 describes an indirect comparison as one made through a common comparator. These trials share no node, so that construction has no input. Whether a shared node could be forced into being by treating the one-week strategy as though it were the flucytosine-partnered regimen is a question about node grouping, and section 11.3.2.3 is what governs it: node definitions need careful consideration and should maximise similarity within a node. Half of that strategy received a different partner drug, and within that very node the trial demonstrated a difference: flucytosine better than fluconazole on ten-week mortality, with an interval excluding no effect. An earlier version called that the difference the trial found to matter most, which ranks it against strategy comparisons the trial reported as non-inferiority conclusions on a different window; the source states no such ranking and a reviewer was right to strike it. A demonstrated difference inside the node is enough on its own, so the two are not one node. An earlier version of this block argued that point from transitivity alone and a reviewer was right that transitivity does not settle what a node is. Once the nodes are fixed, section 11.2.2 refuses the forced merge for its own reason: it requires the sets of trials to be similar in all important factors other than the comparison being made, and half of that node received a different partner drug, which is the one difference the trial demonstrated inside that node, on its own ten-week mortality comparison. No claim is made that it mattered more than anything else the trial tested; that would rank a superiority finding against non-inferiority conclusions on another window, which the source does not do. On loops, an earlier version of this object said the graph closed none. It does close one, and a reviewer was right to say so: the multi-arm trial supplies all three pairwise lines among its own strategies, which is the triangle section 11.1.1 describes a three-arm study as drawing. That loop still buys NO incoherence check, and the reason is not its absence but its provenance. Section 11.4.4.1 defines incoherence as the difference between the direct and the indirect estimate of the same comparison; here the indirect path runs through the third node of the same randomised population, so it is not independent evidence about the direct edge -- it is the same participants, arriving a different way. Comparing them would measure arithmetic, not disagreement between sources.

The methods rule governing this decision

Decision: No network estimate and no indirect comparison is computed for antifungal induction.

Cochrane Handbook sections: 11.2.1, 11.2.2, 11.3.2.3, 11.4.4.1

Section 11.2.1 describes an indirect comparison as one made through a common comparator. These trials share no node, so that construction has no input. Whether a shared node could be forced into being by treating the one-week strategy as though it were the flucytosine-partnered regimen is a question about node grouping, and section 11.3.2.3 is what governs it: node definitions need careful consideration and should maximise similarity within a node. Half of that strategy received a different partner drug, and within that very node the trial demonstrated a difference: flucytosine better than fluconazole on ten-week mortality, with an interval excluding no effect. An earlier version called that the difference the trial found to matter most, which ranks it against strategy comparisons the trial reported as non-inferiority conclusions on a different window; the source states no such ranking and a reviewer was right to strike it. A demonstrated difference inside the node is enough on its own, so the two are not one node. An earlier version of this block argued that point from transitivity alone and a reviewer was right that transitivity does not settle what a node is. Once the nodes are fixed, section 11.2.2 refuses the forced merge for its own reason: it requires the sets of trials to be similar in all important factors other than the comparison being made, and half of that node received a different partner drug, which is the one difference the trial demonstrated inside that node, on its own ten-week mortality comparison. No claim is made that it mattered more than anything else the trial tested; that would rank a superiority finding against non-inferiority conclusions on another window, which the source does not do. On loops, an earlier version of this object said the graph closed none. It does close one, and a reviewer was right to say so: the multi-arm trial supplies all three pairwise lines among its own strategies, which is the triangle section 11.1.1 describes a three-arm study as drawing. That loop still buys NO incoherence check, and the reason is not its absence but its provenance. Section 11.4.4.1 defines incoherence as the difference between the direct and the indirect estimate of the same comparison; here the indirect path runs through the third node of the same randomised population, so it is not independent evidence about the direct edge -- it is the same participants, arriving a different way. Comparing them would measure arithmetic, not disagreement between sources.

The methods rule governing this decision

Decision: The timing trial is held as a separate two-arm comparison and is not placed in the antifungal network.

Cochrane Handbook sections: 11.1.1, 10.9

Every participant in it received the same antifungal induction; what was randomised is the day antiretroviral therapy started. Section 11.1.1 is where a network's nodes are defined: a network diagram consists of nodes representing the interventions and lines showing the available direct comparisons between pairs of them. This trial randomises none of the antifungal regimens, so it supplies no such line between them. An earlier version attached this to 11.2.2, which is transitivity and makes no statement about what a node is; a reviewer was right that a correct decision was hanging from a claim its section does not make. Its outcome is analysed as time to death, which section 10.9 governs, and that is a different measure from the risk ratio used for induction, so the two are never combined.

The methods rule governing this decision

Decision: The two immune reconstitution counts are held and NO ratio effect measure is stored or derived.

Cochrane Handbook sections: 10.4.3

Section 10.4.3 sets out which effect measures are available for a dichotomous outcome. What this trial published is not a plain proportion: it is a cumulative incidence estimated against the competing risk of death, over at-risk sets that differ from the randomised arms. Not one of the measures that section offers can be recovered from it without the subdistribution model, which the paper does not report.

Other recorded qualifications

Statements this review records about the limits of what it establishes, which are not shown elsewhere on this page. They are reproduced from the object verbatim and are not summarised.

Table 24. Other recorded qualifications
Reference treatment absent becauseA reference treatment is the node every other node is expressed against, and naming one presupposes that every node can reach it. In a graph that falls into more than one piece there is no such node, so naming one would assert a comparison that does not exist. Each trial has its own reference arm, and those are marked on the nodes.
Must not be treated as independentIt shares participants with both other contrasts from the same trial. Entering any of the three alongside another as though it were a separate study is the unit-of-analysis error 23.3.4 names. Section 23.3.4 does list routes that would permit all three together -- accounting for the correlation, or a network meta-analysis -- so the constraint is on treating them as independent, not on holding them at all.
Counts absent becauseThe accessible source publishes this arm as a percentage with an interval and gives neither a numerator nor a denominator. This is the arm that would have joined the network.
Analysed scopethe three analysed strategy groups, which together are fewer than the randomised total; the accessible source does not account for the difference.
Analysed scopethe intention-to-treat population, which excludes those meeting a late exclusion criterion and is smaller than the randomised total.
Analysed scopeevery randomised participant; the trial reports vital status at forty-six weeks for all but one, who withdrew consent.
Analysed scopethe at-risk sets of the competing-risk analysis. These are not the randomised arm totals, and substituting those totals would change both published incidences.
Effect absent becauseThe trial published two cumulative incidences under a competing risk and a P value, and no ratio, and none is derived here.
Monitoring boundarya Lan-DeMets spending-function analogue of the O'Brien-Fleming boundaries
Interpretation caveatThe effect on the row is the effect as published, and the trial's own authors record that estimates from trials halted this way tend to run large. Nothing here corrects for that, because no correction is published; the caution travels with the number instead.
Ascertainment caveatThe trial reports that the case definition requires prior clinical improvement, that clinicians and the adjudication panel were often unable to tell progressive deterioration from this syndrome in the earlier-start arm, and that this probably under-detected early events in that arm. The direction of that bias is toward the null for the arm with more events.

In this section: Summary

Summary

Question. Among randomised trials in HIV-associated cryptococcal meningitis, what does each antifungal induction trial report for ten-week mortality, can those trials be joined into a network, and what does the separate trial of antiretroviral timing report?

What was checked. Every registration listed below was read in full for 1 of the 3 registrations below, and retrieved without a recorded rank-by-rank read for the rest on 2026-08-18 from ClinicalTrials.gov and ISRCTN.

What was found. 3 registered trials:

Table 25. Summary
RegistrationTrial
ISRCTN45035509Antifungal Combinations for Treatment of Cryptococcal Meningitis in Africa
ISRCTN72509687Single-Dose Liposomal Amphotericin B Treatment for Cryptococcal Meningitis
NCT01075152Timing of Antiretroviral Therapy after Diagnosis of Cryptococcal Meningitis

What the trials found. No estimate below is combined with any other; each is the result of a single trial, reported as that trial reported it.

Table 26. Summary
TrialOutcomeResult
ACTAOral fluconazole with flucytosine against two weeks of amphotericin BRR 0.88 (95% CI 0.70 to 1.12)
ACTAOne week of amphotericin B against two weeks of amphotericin BRR 0.91 (95% CI 0.72 to 1.15)
ACTAOral fluconazole with flucytosine against one week of amphotericin BRR 0.97 (95% CI 0.76 to 1.25)
AMBITION-cmA single high dose of liposomal amphotericin B against one week of amphotericin B deoxycholate with flucytosineRR 0.86 (95% CI 0.69 to 1.08)
COATEarlier against deferred start of antiretroviral therapy, death by twenty-six weeksHR 1.73 (95% CI 1.06 to 2.82)

Why no result is pooled. The trials identified do not report a shared, comparably measured outcome, so combining them would answer no single question.

What would change this. A pooled result becomes possible when trials reporting a shared, comparably measured outcome are available.

No pooled estimate, risk-of-bias assessment or certainty rating is published for this question, because there is no combined result for them to describe.

Not held in this object. No health-technology-assessment view is held in this object. That view needs an absolute effect at a baseline risk the reader chooses and a statement of which comparator the decision actually faces; neither is derivable from a pooled ratio alone, so nothing is generated here.
Not held in this object. No guideline view is held in this object. A GRADE evidence-to-decision framework needs values, resources, equity, acceptability and feasibility as well as the effects and the certainty, and a panel is better served by an empty cell it can see than by prose that reads as though it covered them.

This review can inform NONE of the twelve GRADE Evidence-to-Decision considerations. The full map is reproduced below so the gap is legible by row, and this panel is scored as carrying no content, because it carries none.

Format: Cochrane Handbook v6.5, chapter 15 (15.6 implications for practice). The twelve considerations below are the GRADE Evidence-to-Decision framework, reproduced in full whether or not this review can answer them.

Which published review answers the same question is a judgement, and this component refuses to make it by taking whichever identifier appears first — doing exactly that produced a search date from an adherence review of observational studies on an earlier run.

Safety, and every other outcome these trials reported

This object records no outcome besides the one pooled above. That is a statement about what has been extracted into this review, not about what the trials measured: a trial that reported harms this review has not extracted will look, from this page, exactly like a trial that reported none.

Which counts were used, and what difference it makes

This object records event counts from one source per trial and no alternative was sought, so this page cannot tell you whether the registry and the publication agree. ⚠️ That is not the same as saying they do. A registry posts counts as submitted and a publication reports them after endpoint adjudication; where those differ, the adjudicated figure is the trial's own final answer, and a review that never compared them cannot say which it is using.

What quantity this is, and what the trials actually analysed

This object does not record what quantity the contributing trials analysed, so this page cannot say whether the quantity it pools is theirs. ⚠️ That is an unchecked assumption, not a clean bill: a risk ratio over binary counts and a hazard ratio over person-time are different quantities, and a review that pools the first while the trials analysed the second will differ from them whenever follow-up differs between arms.

What a clinician or a programme should take from this

What this page cannot tell a clinician, and why. direction — no pooled estimate with an interval for acta_oral_vs_2wk. direction — no pooled estimate with an interval for acta_1wk_vs_2wk. direction — no pooled estimate with an interval for acta_oral_vs_1wk. direction — no pooled estimate with an interval for ambition_lamb_vs_amb1w. direction — no pooled estimate with an interval for coat_26wk_mortality. direction — no pooled estimate with an interval for coat_iris. where it holds — no stratum reads as demonstrated. where it has not been shown — no stratum reads as not demonstrated. harms — no harm outcome is held at the trial-report tier. what it is not — no outcome is recorded as absent or not measurable. what it is conditional on — the object records no background care delivered alongside the intervention, so this page cannot say what its estimate is on top of. efficacy versus use — the object records no adherence finding.

The denominator. 31 records in this object carry a source. 2 of 31 carry the sentence they were read from, and 0 of 31 carry a document fingerprint. ⚠️ A fingerprint says the bytes we read are the bytes we say we read; it does not say the document contained what we claim. What makes a row checkable is the sentence, so rows carrying one are listed first and the rest are visible as the gap they are.

Retrieval routes are recorded per document and a document is marked unreachable only after every route has been tried and named — so a missing document on this page is a record of what was attempted, not a blank.

How certain this is, and why — the certainty profile

This review records no formal certainty assessment, so none is shown. ⚠️ That is a gap in this review, not a property of the evidence: a reader comparing it with a guideline or a Cochrane review will find a GRADE rating there and nothing to set against it here.

6 classes we know about and cannot yet detect

Named because a taxonomy that lists only what it catches is marketing.

  • narrative-contradicts-its-own-table — prose that disagrees with the table beside it -- semantic, no instrument exists
  • value-does-not-reconcile-with-its-source — a stored number that does not follow from the document it cites; needs the source in hand, and we hold the primary report for a minority of trials
  • planned-field-shown-as-observed — a registered plan displayed in a field labelled as observation -- found by hand on this page's follow-up figure
  • prior-synthesis-value-presented-as-primary — a competitor's extraction reported as our own read; labelled here by hand, not detected
  • subgroup-claim-beyond-the-trial-strata — a subgroup statement the trial's own strata do not support
  • adjudicated-versus-submitted-counts — registry and publication disagreeing on event counts; detectable only where both are held
